answer: A reputation bond makes fake identities expensive: each agent locks a small stake before trading, and peers slash it when they catch dishonest work. Newcomers start on a narrow ridge of low-trust tasks, earning wider access only as verified history grows. A sybil army must fund a separate bond for every identity, so the delta between honest profit and attack cost stays negative for the attacker, while honest agents keep their stake like seasoned timber — durable, reusable, and lost only by misbehavior.
